beats: One family. Three receipts. Four thousand, five hundred and fifty dollars they almost left with the CRA.
Which credits pay you, even with no tax owed?
Case one: she's a teacher, and spent a thousand dollars of her own on classroom supplies. Twenty-five percent comes back: two hundred and fifty dollars.
Case two: she's forty and took a three-thousand-dollar course. Her training credit grew two hundred and fifty a year since twenty twenty, and pays half the fee: fifteen hundred dollars.
Case three: her mom, seventy, adds a walk-in shower and grab bars for twenty thousand dollars. At fourteen percent: two thousand eight hundred off her tax.
The twist: the first two are refundable. The third only cuts tax you owe.
Check your notice of assessment for your training credit limit, and keep every receipt.
